summary.en: Israeli airstrikes and artillery shelling have hit southern Lebanese towns such as Nabatieh Heights and Mafdon villages, while an IDF spokesperson visited a Lebanese school, provoking local outrage. Hezbollah continues to expand its arsenal, as evidenced by reports of 14 interdicted arms shipments and an active supply route. Iran has ordered its Revolutionary Guards to leave Beirut strongholds, signaling a shift in regional involvement. The conflict has already caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israels luftangrep og artilleriskudd har rammet sørlige libanesiske byer som Nabatieh Heights og landsbyene i Mafdon, mens en talsmann for IDF besøkte en libanesisk skole, noe som har provosert lokal oppstandelse. Hezbollah fortsetter å utvide sitt arsenal, noe som fremgår av rapporter om 14 avskårne våpensendinger og en aktiv forsyningsrute. Iran har beordret sine revolusjonsgardister til å forlate Beirut-baserte festninger, noe som signaliserer et skifte i regionalt engasjement. Konflikten har allerede forårsaket 4 335 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
